item.title: Clavicular’s Livestream Became Evidence In A Rape Investigation
item.description: Looksmaxxing influencer Braden Peters, known as Clavicular, faces charges over an alleged 2025 assault on a 17-year-old in Massachusetts. Police reviewed livestream footage as part of the investigation. He pleaded not guilty in October 2026 and was released on $10,000 bail.

item.title: Sheila Davalloo Disguised An Attempted Murder As A Game
item.description: In 2003, Sheila Davalloo persuaded her husband to play a blindfolded guessing game, then stabbed him. He survived and later testified at her trial for Anna Lisa Raymundo’s murder. Davalloo received consecutive sentences of 25 years for attempted murder and 50 years for murder.

item.title: Shelly Knotek’s Daughters Exposed The Deaths Inside Her Home
item.description: In 2003, Shelly Knotek’s daughters told police about abuse inside their Washington home. Investigators found Ronald Woodworth buried in the backyard. Knotek entered Alford pleas to murder and manslaughter in the deaths of Kathy Loreno and Woodworth, receiving more than 22 years in prison.

item.title: Charlie Brandt’s Final Killings Exposed A 33-Year Family Secret
item.description: After Charlie Brandt killed his wife, Teri, and niece Michelle Jones in Florida in 2004, then took his own life, his sister revealed an earlier crime: he had killed their mother at 13. That disclosure prompted investigators to examine his past for other unsolved killings.

item.title: A Discarded Cup Linked Stephanie Lazarus To Murder
item.description: DNA from a discarded cup linked LAPD detective Stephanie Lazarus to the 1986 murder of Sherri Rasmussen, her former boyfriend’s wife. The sample matched DNA from a bite wound. Lazarus was convicted in 2012 and sentenced to 27 years to life.

item.title: The Girl Living With The Mauerovás Was Actually 32
item.description: During the 2007 investigation into abuse of two brothers in Kuřim, Czech Republic, authorities discovered that “Anna,” supposedly 13, was adult Barbora Škrlová. In 2008, she received five years in prison; the boys’ mother and aunt received nine and ten years.

item.title: They Killed For A Fortune Corpsewood Manor Never Held
item.description: In December 1982, Charles Scudder and Joseph Odom were murdered at their secluded Georgia home. Avery Brock and Tony West had plotted to steal a fortune they believed was hidden there, but found no cash. Both ultimately received life sentences for the killings.
